start: A member with 120 workouts logged, on Settings → Export & import

user_sees: 'Every workout and set in one file (Hevy’s format). Keep it in Drive or email it to yourself — “Import from Hevy” reads it back.'
must_not: Words that promise Hevy itself can read the file

user_sees: 'Saving…' on the button, then the phone's share sheet titled 'Save my history' with 'mettleup-history-<today>.csv'
must_not: The app freezing on a 5-year history
An older history file offered instead of today's

user_sees: A short success buzz; the file in Drive holds every workout with sets
must_not: Workouts without any set shown as rows

start: A member who saved the file, later on a new phone with no workouts

steps.action: Settings > 'Bring in from Hevy or Strong' > Hevy > 'Choose Hevy file', pick the saved file
user_sees: The preview with the same number of workouts and sets as were saved
Workout names like 'Push · Morning workout' come back with their notes
must_not: Workouts landing at a different clock time (a 6:00 pm workout showing as another hour)

start: A new member with no workout logged

user_sees: 'Nothing to save yet — log a workout first.'

start: A member on a phone where sharing is not available, or where reading the history fails

user_sees: 'Sharing isn’t available on this phone, so the file couldn’t be handed over.' or 'Couldn’t save your history. Please try again.'
must_not: A half-written file left in the phone to be shared later

start: A member who saved the history yesterday and logs one more workout today

user_sees: A new file with today's date that includes today's workout
must_not: Yesterday's file still left in the cache

start: A member signed in to a gym who saves the history

user_sees: The file holds workouts and sets only; the member picks where it goes
must_not: The member's phone number or gym membership in the file
The file sent anywhere without the share sheet
